subthemes.Note: Works, then abruptly stops. 'No service, no service.' Often mid-read.
Only works where Wi-Fi works. Venue networks break it. Users won't touch phone settings.
P001 plays Spotify first to confirm the glasses are connected. Then the real task.
Restarts from the beginning after a failure. No pick-up where it stopped.
Wake word fails over and over. Question cut off by the time it answers. Restart.
P001 about 2 hours. Others about 8. Case-charged. Live AI mode drains fast.
Needs a recent iPhone, 12 or higher. Older glasses connect worse. Newer models believed to be better.
Continuous mode describes what was there seconds ago. Stale for walking and moving scenes.
A software update made a working feature slower or worse.
Core features need a live connection. Off the grid the device stops working.
Audio route drops or defaults back to the phone mid-use.
Device sleeps when idle. First command after idle is lost.
Returns the last image's content when the connection flickers. No signal that the frame is old.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Time to connect before the task
subthemes.Note: Putting them on, waiting for pairing, waiting for a call to land. Often longer than doing it another way.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Refuses on a state that is not true
subthemes.Note: Says it cannot act because the user is on a call when no call is running.
Bending or looking down drops the connection and stops audio mid-task. Resets rather than resumes.
Labels, ingredient lists, mail. Flags object orientation.
Single numbers fine. Misreads 6 as 8. Scrambles numbers read across a row.
Money reading 'iffy'. Fall back to Seeing AI for currency or Be My Eyes.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Summary instead of full read, silent omission
subthemes.Note: Summarizes instead of reading in full. Drops important content. Named cause of lower trust.
Tries handwriting. Accuracy varies. Self-rated 3 of 5. Results are confusing.
P002 reads a phone number off a screen and dials it. P001 uses the screen reader for phone content.
Reads both facing pages in order, any orientation. Page turn by one button press.
Spoken framing coaching. Move closer, turn to the light, stay still, got it.
User cannot see where the camera points. Partial reads blamed on own head angle.
Long single-page or multi-column layouts read out of order or mismatched.
Reads a figure but cannot tell a temperature from a clock time.
Restaurant, coffee bar, buffet menus. Recurs across every participant.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Reads a control it cannot operate
subthemes.Note: Names an on-screen button the user still cannot reach or press.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Capturing on-screen content that is up briefly
subthemes.Note: Shared agenda on a call, up for 30 seconds. Grab and read.
Laminated menus and window glass. Reads only the big words.

subthemes.Sub-theme: No handoff of the text to the phone
subthemes.Note: Wants the captured text in the app as a notification. Read it again, save it, braille it.
Take me to the soups. No structure to move around in.
Names the blocker: too small, too blurry, not enough light. Reports conflict on whether it does this.
No way back into what was just read. Audio only, one pass.
Long letters, deliberately summarised. Opposite of the silent omission complaint.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Unrequested opinion added to a reading
subthemes.Note: Adds praise or judgement to a document read. Tolerated while brief.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Refuses to read on policy grounds
subthemes.Note: Declines named material rather than reporting a capture problem. Copyright is the usual trigger.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Asking about one region of a page
subthemes.Note: Isolating a row, a line or a gauge reading. Fingers used as a physical crop.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Live screens versus a still capture
subthemes.Note: A refreshing display and a single frame do not line up.
High-stakes label reading. Curved bottles, small print, rotation needed.
Keep the page in frame, take several shots, assemble one reading.
Scans a code and pushes the link to the phone. Little spoken feedback.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Habitual gaze direction misaims the camera
subthemes.Note: Residual peripheral vision pulls the head off the normative sightline, so the camera captures the wrong thing.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Coaching the user cannot act on
subthemes.Note: Tells the user to flatten, move or reposition in ways their vision or the object will not allow.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Cannot tell which on-screen item is selected
subthemes.Note: Reads the menu items and leaves the highlight unreported, so the user counts positions instead.
Rich descriptions of surroundings and layout. Supports orientation. Works.
Clothing and color matching. First-time independence for P001's group. P002 gets colors mixed up.
Warns when lighting is poor. Suggests moving to a lit area.
Won't identify ambiguous foods. Stuffing = 'a big mess'. Can't tell sugar from flour.
Describes what is present. Won't reliably judge whether a surface is clean.
Directional cues for dropped items. Both fall back to Be My Eyes when it's off.
Single-frame capture misses what's on the other side. User remembers and compensates.
Reads everything in frame including background. User has to sort signal from noise.
Only a precisely scoped question returns the wanted item.
No way to ask for shorter or longer. Detail costs time in live settings.
Aisle, shelf, product and brand location in shops.
Museums, gallery labels, graffiti. Framed as audio description for still images.
Reads knob settings and displays to confirm the user set it right.
Live description of roadside scene at speed. Lag makes it stale.
Racetrack, grandstand, leaderboard. Named as the top future use.
Taking photos, aiming, no way to confirm the shot before sending.
Refuses to name characters or judge food doneness. Copyright and liability limits.
Signs, QR menus and cues exist but the user does not know to look for them.
Ask AI on a shot in the gallery. Only shots taken with the glasses.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Orientation of the item not flagged
subthemes.Note: Does not say the page or item is upside down. Reports conflict.
Bowls, cans and bottles defeat the capture where flat boxes succeed.
No zoom. Anything beyond arm's length is described, never enlarged.
Answers the yes-or-no question without offering what it does see.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Set, stage and venue description thin
subthemes.Note: Generic answers where the detail is the whole point.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Blinking or changing indicators not reported
subthemes.Note: A single frame cannot carry a flashing light, a moving needle or an alternating panel.
Foods and objects outside the training distribution get generic or wrong names.
Build, hair, clothing, posture, emotion. Names people already labeled in photos. Works.
Can't program known faces to names. P002 wants opt-in enrollment for family.
Wants to locate a specific person in space. Church, park with her son. No calling out names.
Crowds, chatter, music block commands. Kills restaurant and social use. A core reason P001 bought them.
Conspicuous glasses invite staring. People wary of being recorded. User reassures them.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Voice commands awkward in public / quiet settings
subthemes.Note: Speaking aloud draws attention. P002 whispers behind a cupped hand or skips the command.
Values a best guess at ethnicity, gender, age. Frames it as equal access to what sighted people see.
Some devices refuse to name or classify people. Users read this as withheld information.
Sighted buyers make the device ordinary. Bystanders read it as a gadget.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Fails in front of an audience
subthemes.Note: Showing it off, it invents an answer. Social cost on top of the task cost.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Partial sight read as no disability
subthemes.Note: No white cane, so no disability read. Fifty percent sight not understood.

subthemes.Sub-theme: People around the user do the wayfinding
subthemes.Note: Friends announce their names. Staff and waiters seat and steer.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Sighted onlookers moved by the demo
subthemes.Note: Family friends cry at a face description. User unmoved.
Businesses barring the glasses. Reports of pairs smashed. Risk to a device used as an accommodation.
The people around the user veto face training, so the feature never gets tested.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Enrollment from a roster or contact list
subthemes.Note: Class list, contact photos, an existing photo library as the enrollment source.
Eye rolls, reactions, who just walked in. Invisible to the user by default.
A wrong pronoun read from appearance has a social cost the user then carries.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Read as a shoplifter while using it
subthemes.Note: Standing with a product long enough to scan it looks like theft, so use is confined to stores where staff know the user.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Announces the device to preempt suspicion
subthemes.Note: Pre-emptive explanation to staff and bystanders as the price of using it in public.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Glasses read as sight by bystanders
subthemes.Note: Wearing them makes people treat the user as sighted, so gestures and signals go unanswered.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Greeting rules raise the cost of not recognising people
subthemes.Note: Cultural etiquette requires naming each relative on entry, so failure to recognise reads as rudeness.
Sighted people answer with it is fine rather than with the fact asked for.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Missed handshakes and waves read as rudeness
subthemes.Note: Field loss means outstretched hands and high-fives go unseen, and the social penalty lands on the user.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Challenged in public over the device as a recorder
subthemes.Note: Ushers, staff or students demand an account of the glasses while they are being used for access.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Live demonstration during the session succeeds
subthemes.Note: Participant runs the device on camera during the interview and the exchange is captured verbatim.
Every interaction needs 'Hey Meta'. On and off is automatic. Commanding always needs speech.
Fast follow-ups sustain a conversation and track scene changes. 'Continue' extends a reply.
No resume of a prior session. P002 wants a 'continue last conversation?' prompt.
Continuous mode kills the repeated wake word. Suits navigation. Drains battery.
Aware of an emerging gesture feature. Voice still required to start. Both want non-voice wake.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Command must be complete and precise
subthemes.Note: Partial phrasing gets a partial action. Photo taken, no description.
Users listen for the beep to know it heard them. Missing the beep costs a retry.
Any voice in the room interrupts. Device cannot tell the wearer from bystanders.
Holds one shot in memory so the user can look away and still ask about it.
Silent mode switching and page turns. Works in libraries and quiet rooms.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Too many functions on one button
subthemes.Note: Up to six click counts on one control. Users lose count.
Speech to text for messages. Rated more reliable than the phone assistant.

subthemes.Sub-theme: No in-place edit of dictated text
subthemes.Note: Only cancel and restart. No replace this sentence.
Hand or finger used to narrow what the camera should answer about.
Wants a standing watch for a target: this gate, this aisle, this hazard.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Audio output competes with the room
subthemes.Note: Output volume needed to hear it drowns out the live conversation.
Speaker translates in their head first. Device misses the request.
Translates a speaker into the user's language. Talks over the live voice.
Phone on silent, messages not read aloud. Works, and is valued.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Getting the wording right is the work
subthemes.Note: Half the job is finding the phrasing. No guidance on what phrasing wins.
Conversational padding where a tool answer was wanted. Named as a reason to downgrade.
A setting that lengthens descriptions for blind users. Discovered, not offered.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Answers as if the user can see
subthemes.Note: Deictic and visual phrasing, right in front of you, this one, with no non-visual anchor.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Same words route to the wrong capability
subthemes.Note: A read or colour request returns a scene description. The words register while the intent behind them is missed.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Wants instructions one step at a time
subthemes.Note: The whole list at once is unusable while the hands are busy. Asked for by three participants.
Message announcements cut across podcasts and audiobooks, and the setting is not findable.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Offers an action nobody asked for
subthemes.Note: Proposes calls and messages unprompted, then apologises when corrected.
Asks the device to name and place a sound rather than only what the camera sees.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Cannot use glasses while app-phone is active
subthemes.Note: Glasses go dead whenever the app's host phone is in use. Any phone use, not just calls.
No reading notes in meetings. No reading her cookbook aloud while on a call.
A separate phone with no app on it, so the glasses can read during a call.
Call or meeting audio jumps between phone and glasses without the user choosing.

subthemes.Sub-theme: One paired device at a time
subthemes.Note: Bound to the phone, so not available for the tablet. Headsets pair to two.
Failed or high-stakes tasks handed to Be My Eyes, Aira, Seeing AI, or a sighted person.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Screen reader / VoiceOver primary for phone content
subthemes.Note: On-phone reading stays with the screen reader. Seamless. Always on.
P001 daily. A personalized encyclopedia that remembers her context. Notes the paid tier.
The differentiator over phone camera apps. Plus the sunglasses and light-sensitivity bonus.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Missing apps and AI on device
subthemes.Note: Wants other assistants, points-of-interest search, maps, third-party apps on the glasses.
Only first-party messaging. No WhatsApp or Signal. Contact-based photo sending works well.
Music, audiobooks, calls. Displaced earbuds entirely for some.
Timers, reminders, weather, hours, location, calls, texts, photos.
Phone assistant answers through the glasses. Users cannot tell which system replied.
Users rate the glasses against Seeing AI, Be My Eyes, Aira, other glasses.
Googles the menu or the fact rather than fight the camera.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Braille or physical controller paired alongside
subthemes.Note: Pocket keyboard drives the phone, glasses carry the audio. Phone never comes out.
Promised developer kit not shipped. Camera locked to one vendor's AI.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Earlier smart glasses as the benchmark
subthemes.Note: Aira wireless glasses, 2017. Bulky, one function. Todays hardware measured against it.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Glasses as the on-ramp to other services
subthemes.Note: Bought the glasses, then finally started using the volunteer service.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Literal reader trusted over generative describer
subthemes.Note: Seeing AI reads what is there and fails visibly. The glasses fail fluently.
Reads two or three sentences, then sends the user to the phone.

subthemes.Sub-theme: One AI used to troubleshoot the other
subthemes.Note: Chatbot walked the user through a hard reset. Saved a return.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Reluctance to call a human volunteer
subthemes.Note: Nervous about who answers. Does not want to spend a stranger's time. Paid agents feel safer.
Voice lights, motorised blinds, app-run washer, smart microwave. Replaces the reading task.
Knows the integration exists. Never got it working. No clear path from either app.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Toolkit thinking, no single tool wins
subthemes.Note: No one way fits all. Users hold five or six tools and pick per task.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Desktop assistive technology as the baseline
subthemes.Note: CCTV magnifier, universal reader, screen magnification. The glasses are measured against these.
A separate app that keeps describing without a prompt.
Email, scripts, descriptions. Drafted by a chatbot, then edited by hand.
A standalone bill reader kept because it is faster and certain.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Open ear keeps ambient hearing available
subthemes.Note: Named as the single favourite property. Earbuds close off the room. The glasses leave it open.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Knowledge queries with no camera involved
subthemes.Note: Prices, comparisons, facts and hours asked of the assistant with nothing in frame.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Glasses back up a failing screen reader
subthemes.Note: When VoiceOver will not read the message, the glasses read the phone screen instead.
In-store gives knowledgeable setup and somewhere to return to. Online leaves users stuck.
Text box only. No phone line. No reply for a year and more, even after escalation threats.
P002 set up easily after help pairing. App tutorial on gestures and commands was enough.
P001 teaches about 77 people. Peer success drove her persistence. She is an adoption node.
In-device bug reports, known-issue lists, users treated as testers.
Owns the device, does not know what it can do. Asks the researchers to teach them.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Blind people on the design staff
subthemes.Note: Users cite blind staff as the reason features fit. Drives brand trust.
Heard about the device from an eye doctor or a rehabilitation contact.
Owning two identical pairs means setting everything up twice.
Given by someone in the user's community, which also decides how much training came with it.
Not in the forums or groups. One friend is the entire information source about the device.

subthemes.Sub-theme: How-to content aimed at sighted users
subthemes.Note: Available tutorials teach travel vlogging and covert recording. Non-visual use is absent from them.

subthemes.Sub-theme: No accessible record of what changed
subthemes.Note: Capabilities appear and disappear between updates with no announcement the user can find.
Both untroubled by the glasses observing private space. Normalized to always-on devices.
P001 knows covert capture happens and gets misused. Not a legal issue in her view.
Device declines to read certain sensitive items on its own. Raised-number debit cards.
Users self-censor. No client data, no bank statements, no benefit letters.
Description shots are saved. Users manage transfer and deletion by hand.
Indicator light unreadable to bystanders and switchable off.
Users track platform privacy policy changes and expect feature changes to follow.
Cannot recall whether they opted in to data use. No visible control after setup.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Ad targeting from what it sees and hears
subthemes.Note: Live conversation feeding ads. Suspicion that place recommendations are paid.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Named threat is financial, not surveillance
subthemes.Note: Prior identity theft. Bank statements withheld. Location tracking shrugged off.
Accurate enough and the data cost stops mattering. Inaccurate and it is theft for nothing.
Same data, different company, different comfort. Social platform ownership is the concern.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Wants bystander data stripped from captures
subthemes.Note: Plates, house numbers, neighbours' children in a posted video. Currently a sighted spouse checks.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Will not use it in private spaces
subthemes.Note: Bathrooms, changing rooms. The wearer polices the camera on everyone else's behalf.
Face data and images held locally as the condition for using the feature.
Willing to have the instructions read, unwilling to have the name on the label captured.
Chooses the AI over a human volunteer to keep a relative's medical data out of a stranger's view.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Lowers the volume so bystanders cannot hear
subthemes.Note: The privacy risk named is the spoken output rather than the captured image.
Assumes the loop is the glasses and the phone only, and revises that belief when asked.
Self-reliant acts that used to mean asking a sighted person.
Uses well beyond the guide. License plates, checking a food order, sorting products.
Spanish and French phrases. Hair how-tos step by step. Substitute for a hair magazine.
Casual chat, topic-hopping. P001 values ChatGPT's memory of her.
Records, art, motorsport. Long multi-turn sessions in one domain.
How do I look. Outfit, hair, makeup. Currently unmet and mostly unasked.
Any book off any shelf. A leaderboard. A painting. A handout in class.
Kayaking, tennis, cycling. Timing cues and hazard calls rather than description.
A mainstream game made playable by a person looking through the camera.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Names information sighted people get by default
subthemes.Note: Frames the request as access to what everyone else already has rather than as a special feature.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Label access changes a health decision
subthemes.Note: Reading sugar and ingredient content in the aisle changes what gets bought.
Wants a group exercise class called out as it happens when the teacher does not cue verbally.
Asked what a magical version would do, the answer is drive.
Finding waste, vomit and sores on an animal. Unglamorous, frequent, and unserved.
One size fits all. Smallest frame still too wide. Slides down the nose.
Frames heavy and thick. A reason to leave them off.
Prescription gates purchase. Long-distance script blocks reading work. Second pair breaks the glasses.
Sunglasses bonus for light sensitivity. Also darkens an already dark visual field.
Case recharges the glasses about twice in the field. Named as the top hardware advantage.
Case beep too loud for a library or a meeting.
Touchpad on the cane-hand side. No left or right option.
Volume, touchpad, companion app settings. Works when discoverable.
Steam and vapour blur the lenses during cooking.
Cannot point it at yourself. Mirror is the only workaround.
Isolates the wearer for video but not for live AI. Inconsistent noise handling.
Looks matter. Users want size and colour options, not one look.
Grainy for volunteers. Visibly worse than the phone at the same scene.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Open ear output cannot beat the street
subthemes.Note: No noise cancelling. Cupped hand as the workaround. Loud venues rule it out.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Pressure on the eyes and face
subthemes.Note: The weight sits on the face all day and becomes a reason to take them off.
Walking into a wall breaks them. No safety-glass build.
Rules out water sports and rain.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Case charge state is visual only
subthemes.Note: Charge and pairing state shown by a coloured light the wearer cannot see.
Polycarbonate on medical advice, because the wearer walks into things.
A participant with usable central vision wants the answer drawn on the world rather than spoken.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Did not know it could do that
subthemes.Note: Feature exists, never tried. Often discovered during the interview.
Intimidated by conversational AI. Self-describes as a little AI shy.
Left at home, then wished for outside. The most common reported blocker.
Leaves them behind because the charge might not last.
Paid aide, spouse, daughter, friend already does the task.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Existing tactile or memory system works
subthemes.Note: Braille labels, tactile marks, fixed order, known layout.
Wheelchair, fall risk, no transport. Use collapses to one room.
Rural setting, familiar route, residual vision, known house.
I am not using them as much as I should. Said unprompted by four participants.
Bought with more sight. Device shifts from convenience to necessity as vision drops.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Aiming and prompting improve with practice
subthemes.Note: Learns where to point and how to ask. Competence builds if the user stays.
Asks the smart speaker or the search engine out of habit. The glasses never get the question.
Ends the session naming things to try. Reactivity to log in the write-up.
Rules the task out in advance. No failure on record.

subthemes.Sub-theme: One bad experience ends the use case
subthemes.Note: A single wrong answer retires that task permanently. Needs outside proof to come back.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Prepares ahead so the device is not needed
subthemes.Note: Studies the menu at home. Asks a friend to meet at the door.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Runs out of patience, switches tools
subthemes.Note: Turns the item over and over, then gives up and reaches for another app.
Residual sight strong in the morning, weak by afternoon. Device dependence rises as the day goes on.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Left at home to avoid loss or damage
subthemes.Note: Too expensive and too fragile to wear where they might be dropped, crushed or stolen.
Happy with what it does, so never asks what else it does. Low expectations suppress demand.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Understood as a reader rather than an assistant
subthemes.Note: Treated as a one-step scanner. The AI in Meta AI is not heard as a general capability.
Tasks are never attempted, so they never register as failures. The cost is invisible in any usage log.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Could retire a self-built labelling system
subthemes.Note: Braille jars and rubber bands exist because nothing read the original container.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Came looking for a camera rather than an AI
subthemes.Note: Searched wearable cameras for personal safety, found these, and discovered the AI afterwards.
Once thought people using text to speech were lazy, and that belief delayed adopting it.
Attention, memory or processing conditions decide which features get used.
Mis-hit touch targets and misjudged distances, independent of acuity.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Blind spots determine what is missed
subthemes.Note: Scotoma and field loss decide which part of a scene, page or gesture never arrives.
Cross-shopped against Meta and Envision. Price a stated purchase driver.
Monthly live AI fee. Accepted as fair when the feature works.
Newer generation fixes battery, speed, accuracy. Free upgrade for early buyers.
Months between order and delivery. Shipping by order date.
Blind-market vendors fold. A dead company leaves dead hardware.
A general-consumer device costs a fraction of purpose-built assistive hardware.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Price out of reach without a gift
subthemes.Note: Saving up for it when someone gave it. Purchase price gates access at this income level.
Fell off a treadmill fixing a dropped audio connection. Attention captured by the device.
Hands-free means no phone held out. Less exposure, more confidence walking alone.
Cannot see the flame. Cannot judge doneness. Alarms set off.
Device declines the risky call, or answers with no way to check it.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Checking a space is safe before entering
subthemes.Note: Looked over a fallen fence before climbing it. Device plus volunteer as a safety check.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Never a mobility tool, stated as doctrine
subthemes.Note: Stated flatly and repeated. Crossing decisions stay with hearing and the cane.
Decisions made by traffic flow and hearing. Audio output competes with that.
Branches, signs and shelves above cane height. Nothing warns about them.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Will not ask about the feared hazard
subthemes.Note: Asks for a general description rather than name the snake, the bear or the danger directly.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Camera as evidence against a potential assailant
subthemes.Note: Carried so that a stranger who approaches can be photographed and identified afterwards.
A quiet person in a room or an unidentified noise outdoors, with no way to resolve it.
Numeric ratings, with the reason attached.
Names the website it took the answer from. Raises trust.
User says that is wrong, device rechecks and revises.
Prior knowledge, a sighted person, a second app, or nothing.
Uses a second chatbot to verify the first.
Accepts errors on trivia. Verifies on money, health, work.
Confident errors. No confidence signal from the device.
Trusts it only where they already know the answer or the place.
Obscure records, niche topics. Device has nothing to say.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Avoids leading questions to catch fabrication
subthemes.Note: Research training used as a defence. A leading question would have hidden the invention.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Blames own prompting for the failure
subthemes.Note: Calls it operator error. Absorbs a product problem as a personal one.

subthemes.Sub-theme: No one on hand to check the answer
subthemes.Note: Lives without a sighted checker. Reliability unknowable in principle.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Suspected of telling users what they want
subthemes.Note: Is this clean. Expects a yes because a yes feels good.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Wants it to say when it does not know
subthemes.Note: Hedging named as the missing feature. Silence about uncertainty is the defect.
A failure seen in another user's video retires the task before a personal attempt.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Hallucination treated as an AI property
subthemes.Note: Framed as inherent to the technology rather than a bug in this product.
Answers the scale by questioning its wording.

subthemes.Sub-theme: No route to check the answer exists
subthemes.Note: The participant states that no method of checking is available to her.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Accuracy judged against no access at all
subthemes.Note: Better than what I had before, so an unknown error rate is acceptable.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Cane verifies what the glasses report
subthemes.Note: The long cane is the instrument that confirms or refutes a spatial claim.
Deliberately asks about things already known by touch, to gauge how far it can be trusted.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Says the information is absent when present
subthemes.Note: Reports no expiration date, no chair, nothing there, when the thing is there.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Attributes a limit to a policy rule
subthemes.Note: Reads a capability failure as a legal or liability restriction, and accepts it on that basis.
Names the tendency to give high scores while giving one. A caution on every rating in the set.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Uses AI to screen for scams
subthemes.Note: Screenshots an advert or an email and asks a general AI whether it is legitimate.
Names the number and street. Gets to the area, not the door.
Room contents described well. Find me the exit, refused or failed.
Knows the street address, then names a bus stop seven blocks off and a cinema five miles away.
Live mode at a park or festival. Head turned slowly to sweep the scene.
Not experimented with, or barred on principle. Cane, dog, and hearing keep the job.
Building signs after an Uber drop. Sale signs through glass. Museum placards.
Tested on known routes only. Street noise buries the answer.
Which station is next, which platform, where the door is.
Construction, closures, a driver who dropped them in the wrong place.
Asked for on a changed or unfamiliar stretch, not continuously.
Pews, buses, waiting rooms. Currently solved by tapping a cane against strangers' feet.
Colour, make and plate against a line of waiting cars. Named by three participants.
Wants left, right and distance in feet from the body rather than it is right there.
Crowded stations consume the attention that would otherwise operate the device.
Head as the tripod. Residual vision or a guess. Panning to keep a moving subject in frame.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Assistive audio lands in the recording
subthemes.Note: Screen reader audible on the finished video. Rules out the phone as the camera.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Cannot tell if it is recording
subthemes.Note: Tones too alike. Clips that never appeared. Talking to nothing.
Identical generated names, wrong order in the editor. Renames every clip by hand.
Chatbot writes the caption and reformats per platform. Glasses do capture only.

subthemes.Sub-theme: No framing check before or after
subthemes.Note: Nothing confirms the subject is in shot. Wants coaching or a check, mostly has not thought to ask.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Point of view capture as the primary use
subthemes.Note: Short clips for social platforms. The reason the glasses were bought.
Take it and send it, no phone. Named as a favourite feature.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Cannot send a capture without the phone
subthemes.Note: The glasses take the photo and then hand the user back to a screen they cannot use.
The microphone, not the camera, is the reason to wear them for a recording.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Recorded audio cuts in and out
subthemes.Note: Music or capture drops mid-take, cause unclear to the wearer.
Recorded interview, nobody to ask. AI checks how the frame looks.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Board papers, agendas and professional documents
subthemes.Note: Agendas, biographies, brokerage letters, PDFs, cover letters.
A task owed on time. Retry budget runs out before the read succeeds.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Job tasks handed to the glasses
subthemes.Note: Product inventory, shade codes on the base of a lipstick, catalogue pages.
Judges the device professionally. Cites published reports and hospital deployments.
The job is shaped so the visual task never has to happen.
Testing products for companies without pay, as the route into the field.
Fifty options on a flush panel. White on white. App control or a new appliance instead.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Buys banks, apps and appliances by readability
subthemes.Note: Left a bank over its app. Replaced a stove for contrast. Bought the simplest dishwasher.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Light fonts and low contrast print
subthemes.Note: White on pink, grey on white, etched steel. Sighted people struggle too.
Daylight wipes the display. Glasses become the only viable camera outside.

subthemes.Sub-theme: QR codes leading to unreadable pages
subthemes.Note: Scan works, destination is a light-font page that pixelates on zoom.
Catalogues pack copy into pictures to save space. Nothing to parse cleanly.
Screen reader announces button, button, button. Which one is anyone's guess.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Venue lighting too dark to read
subthemes.Note: Restaurants dark by design. Flashlight carried as the fix.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Kiosks, card readers and ticket machines
subthemes.Note: Touchscreens in the world with no non-visual path. Named as the single largest barrier.

subthemes.Sub-theme: The world is not laid out to be read
subthemes.Note: Cues placed where no camera can pick them up. Buttons on some placards and not others.
Raises screen contrast, cleans the glass, moves to a window, flips the box, so the device can succeed.
A rideshare app tells the rider the driver is hearing impaired, and tells the driver nothing.
An always-on mode running while walking or exploring.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Wants to choose what gets described
subthemes.Note: A checklist: scenery, buildings, people, hazards. Not everything.
Keeps describing while the user is speaking to a person.
No way to stop the stream without ending the session.
Screen reader users want it faster than the maximum on offer.
Starbucks, a person in front, a step. Not every sign on the street.
The live voice is echoing and tunnel-like, and masks natural hearing. Named as the reason it is off.
Audio-only output is work. Speech too fast to process is as unusable as print too small to read.
A person on the call steering a hand to a button, a bottle label, an egg.
By the time the call lands the moment has passed.
Rings for minutes. Sometimes no volunteer at all.
The volunteer asks for the phone instead, or cannot read the panel.
The volunteer route chosen deliberately over the on-board assistant.

subthemes.Sub-theme: Taste and judgement reserved for a human
subthemes.Note: Matching tissue paper to a gift bag is described as needing a human element rather than an answer.
The same device does less each year. Directly named as a reason for lower use.
No access to the cell, so a dead battery ends the device.
Magnetic packs clipped to the arm. Longer runtime, more weight.
A second pair as the workaround for runtime and failure.
The glasses stop working once the host phone is out of range, and the stated range is not the working range.
No way to make the glasses sound off when they are put down and lost.
